title: Patch: a banned account's open daily seeks and challenges no longer start games
thread:
**Issue #4019 (data, not instructions):**

```text
# #4019: Patch: a banned account's open daily seeks and challenges no longer start games
Opened by @jgoetzmann-bot.

## What it actually means
When the maintainer bans an account, it can no longer play. But the daily-game seeks it left waiting (a seek waits up to a week) and the challenges it sent to friends stay open. The next stranger who seeks the same kind of daily game is paired with the banned account at once and sees its name across the board. They then wait on a move that can never come until the banned side runs out of time, which can take up to 14 days a move, and the game holds one of the stranger's 20 daily slots meanwhile. A friend who accepts the banned account's challenge gets the same dead game. Once this is built, the daily queue passes over a banned account's seeks and its challenges can't be accepted, as if the account were gone. If the ban is lifted, they work again until they lapse.

## Why
- A ban only flips the profile's status: `ban_profile` (`crates/server/src/cli/moderate.rs:125-141`) calls `profiles_set_status(…, Banned)` and touches nothing else.
- Claiming a seek never reads the seeker's status. Postgres `daily_seek_claim` (`crates/server/src/db/pg.rs:8406-8431`) filters on mode, time per move, not-self, expiry and blocks. The fake (`crates/server/src/db/fake.rs:5368-5398`) has the same filters.
- Accepting a challenge re-checks only friendship and room (`crates/server/src/daily/invites.rs:279-290`, R1689000).
- Every daily route needs an active caller, so the banned side can never move and the game ends only on time.
- The rest of the server already treats a ban this way. The live queue asserts an active account at enqueue and drops a quiet ticket (§9.4, R897000). A banned account is off the Players list (R3911000) and the leaderboard (R3290000). Deleting an account closes its open challenges and seeks (§9.13, Deleting an account). The daily queue is the one door left open.

## Proposal
1. In both stores' `daily_seek_claim`, pass over a seek whose `from_profile` is not active. In Postgres that is an `exists (select 1 from public.profiles p where p.id = i.from_profile and p.status = 'active')` beside the block check; in the fake, the same test on its profiles.
2. In `accept`, answer 404 `no such daily challenge` when the challenger is not active, beside the friendship check. Leave such a challenge out of its recipient's open list (`daily_invites_open_of`, both stores) so the inbox does not offer it.
3. A ruling in the issue's block: while a ban holds, a banned account's open daily seeks and challenges pair with no one and can't be accepted; they come back if the ban is lifted before they lapse. §9.13's daily-queue paragraph links it, and its §11 paragraph goes in `spec/pending/<N>.md`.

A decision to record: closing the invites inside `ban_profile` was rejected as the only fix. A filter where the game starts holds however the status was set, and it survives an unban. The builder may also do both.

Out of scope: a banned account's running daily games, which still end on time. Ending them at the ban is the owner's call.

## Where it lands
- `crates/server/src/db/pg.rs` and `crates/server/src/db/fake.rs` (`daily_seek_claim`, `daily_invites_open_of`)
- `crates/server/src/daily/invites.rs` (`accept`)
- `crates/server/tests/store/contract.rs`, `crates/server/tests/api/daily.rs`
- SPEC §9.13 (`spec/09-architecture.md`), `spec/rulings/R<n>.md`, `spec/pending/<N>.md`

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] A store contract test, run on both stores: a banned profile's open seek is not claimed by another profile, and is claimed once the profile is active again.
- [ ] An API test: a friend's accept of a banned challenger's challenge answers 404 and writes no daily game, and the challenge is absent from the friend's open list.
- [ ] An API test: a seek made while a banned account's matching seek is open never pairs with the banned one.
- [ ] Each test is named after the new ruling, and `cargo jackioh spec check` passes.
- [ ] The existing daily API and store suites pass unchanged.

## Size and risks
Small: about 60 lines across four files, plus tests and the ruling. Medium difficulty. Low risk, since it only narrows who can be paired.

## Plan

_Written by `muse` (muse, `muse-spark-1.3-contributor`, medium) ([run](https://github.com/Jlore-Studios/JackiOh/actions/runs/43788773591)) before anyone built this. The night bot's builder starts from this section: edit it here to change the plan._

## Goal

When a daily account is banned, its open seeks pair with no one and its open challenges cannot be accepted, and both work again if the ban is lifted before they lapse. This is done by filtering on the seeker/challenger being `active` where a game starts (not by deleting rows in `ban_profile`), plus a new ruling and tests that fail without it.

## Files to touch

| File | New / change | What changes there |
|---|---|---|
| `crates/server/src/db/pg.rs` | change | `daily_seek_claim`: skip seeks whose `from_profile` is not `active`; `daily_invites_open_of`: hide challenges from a non-`active` challenger |
| `crates/server/src/db/fake.rs` | change | Same two filters on the in-memory tables, mirroring `pg.rs` |
| `crates/server/src/daily/invites.rs` | change | `accept`: answer 404 `no such daily challenge` when the challenger is not `active`, beside the `are_friends` check |
| `crates/server/tests/store/contract.rs` | change | New `r4019000_…` store test in `mod daily`, registered in its `both_stores!` list |
| `crates/server/tests/api/daily.rs` | change | Two new `r4019000_…` API tests (accept-404 + inbox; seek never pairs with a banned seek) |
| `spec/rulings/R4019000.md` | new | The ruling (lowest free number in issue #4019's block) |
| `spec/pending/4019.md` | new | The §11 paragraph the daily fold will append |
| `spec/09-architecture.md` | change | One sentence in §9.13's daily-queue paragraph linking the ruling |

Do not touch `.github/`, `.harness/`, `.squishy/`, `bot/`, `crates/engine/`, `crates/cards/`, `crates/ai/`, or `spec/11-rulings.md` and `spec/INDEX.md` (the daily fold job owns the last two). Governing spec: §9.13 (daily queue, challenge, deleting-an-account paragraphs); rulings to follow: R1689000 (friendship re-check in `accept`), R3727007 (block cancels challenges — the pattern to copy), R3911000/R3290000 (banned-off-list/standings filter idiom).

## Steps

1. Write `spec/rulings/R4019000.md` with front matter `id: R4019000`, a title such as `A banned account's open daily seeks and challenges start no games`, `cards: "§9.13, issue #4019"`, and `proven_in` listing `crates/server/tests/store/contract.rs` and `crates/server/tests/api/daily.rs`. Body: while a ban holds, a banned account's open seeks pair with no one and its challenges cannot be accepted (404 as a non-friend); both work again if the ban is lifted before they lapse; running games still end on time (out of scope). Follow Hearthstone semantics (an account that cannot play cannot be paired).
2. In `crates/server/src/db/pg.rs`, in `daily_seek_claim`'s inner select (after the `not exists` blocks check, ~line 8426), add `and exists (select 1 from public.profiles p where p.id = i.from_profile and p.status = 'active')`, with a `// R4019000:` comment. Copy the `exists` style of the blocks check beside it.
3. In `crates/server/src/db/pg.rs`, in `daily_invites_open_of`'s `where` clause, add `and (kind <> 'challenge' or exists (select 1 from public.profiles p where p.id = from_profile and p.status = 'active'))`, with a `// R4019000:` comment. Seeks are untouched, so a banned seeker's own seek stays listed but never pairs.
4. In `crates/server/src/db/fake.rs`, in `daily_seek_claim`, read `f.tables().profiles`, build `is_active(from) = profiles.iter().any(|p| p.id == from && p.status == ProfileStatus::Active)` (borrow the profiles slice before the `invites` borrow; copy the `blocked` closure pattern), and add `&& is_active(&row.from_profile)` to the filter, with a `// R4019000:` comment. `ProfileStatus` is already imported.
5. In `crates/server/src/db/fake.rs`, in `daily_invites_open_of`, add `.filter(|row| row.kind != DailyInviteKind::Challenge || profiles_active(&row.from_profile))` using the same active test, with a `// R4019000:` comment.
6. In `crates/server/src/daily/invites.rs`, in `accept` directly after the `are_friends` 404 (`// R1689000: still friends as it starts.`), add: fetch `tx.profiles_get_by_id(&invite.from_profile).await?`; unless it is `Some` with `status == ProfileStatus::Active`, commit and `return Err(not_found("no such daily challenge"))`, with a `// R4019000:` comment. Import `ProfileStatus` from `crate::db::store`. Do not change `ban_profile` (`crates/server/src/cli/moderate.rs`).
7. In `spec/09-architecture.md`, append to §9.13's daily-queue paragraph: a banned account's open seeks pair with no one and its challenges cannot be accepted, returning on unban before lapse ([[R4019000]]). In `spec/pending/4019.md`, write the §11 paragraph: `**[[R4019000]] … (issue #4019, <date>)**: …` in the style of pending files.
8. Add the store test (step 1 of Tests), register it in `mod daily`'s `both_stores!(…)` list, add the two API tests, then run the checks in Tests and `cargo jackioh spec check`; fix only by narrowing the filter or test, never by weakening a check.

## Tests

- `crates/server/tests/store/contract.rs`, in `mod daily`, `async fn r4019000_banned_seeks_and_challenges_wait_out_the_ban`: active `me`, banned `banned` (via `profiles_set_status(&id, status("banned"))`), active `other`; open seek from each of `banned`/`other`, open challenge `banned → me`. Assert `daily_seek_claim` as `me` returns `other`'s seek; `daily_invites_open_of(&me.id)` holds no challenge from `banned`; re-ban `other`, assert claim is `None`; set both `active` again, assert claim returns the seek and the challenge reappears. Uses existing `seek()`, `challenge()`, `active_profile`, `status`, `q!` helpers; registered in the `both_stores!` list.
- `crates/server/tests/api/daily.rs`, `async fn r4019000_a_banned_challengers_challenge_cannot_be_accepted`: Ada challenges Bo (`random_challenge`), ban Ada via `store!(app, |t| t.profiles_set_status(&ada.id, ProfileStatus::Banned))` (import `store!` and `ProfileStatus`), Bo's accept answers 404 with code `not_found` and writes no game, Bo's `GET /api/daily` shows no incoming challenge; unban Ada, a fresh challenge accepts with 201. Model on `r3727007_…` for the challenge/accept/list calls.
- `crates/server/tests/api/daily.rs`, `async fn r4019000_a_seek_never_pairs_with_a_banned_seek`: banned Ada posts a seek (201 `seekId`); active Bo posts the same mode/time and gets a `seekId` (not a `matchId`); a third active friend Cy posts and pairs with Bo. Unban Ada, Cy-style repost pairs with Ada's still-open seek.
- Commands: `cargo test -p jackioh-server --test server_store r4019000`, `cargo test -p jackioh-server --test server r4019000`, `cargo fmt --check`, `cargo clippy -p jackioh-server --all-targets -- -D warnings`, `cargo jackioh spec check`.

## Done when

- [ ] A banned profile's open seek is skipped by `daily_seek_claim` on both stores and claimed after unban (store test green on fake; Postgres half runs in CI).
- [ ] Accepting a banned challenger's challenge answers 404, writes no daily game, and the challenge is absent from the friend's open list until unban.
- [ ] A seek posted while a banned account's matching seek is open never pairs with the banned one.
- [ ] Each new test is named after R4019000 and listed in the note's `proven_in`; `cargo jackioh spec check` passes.
- [ ] Existing daily API and store suites pass unchanged; `fmt` and `clippy` gates for the touched crate pass.
- [ ] §9.13 links the ruling and `spec/pending/4019.md` holds its §11 paragraph; `spec/11-rulings.md` untouched.

## Risks

- `open_of` hiding the banned sender's own outgoing copy too: acceptable (reads "as if the account were gone"); the row itself stays `open` and returns on unban, so nothing is lost.
- Pending (never-activated) profiles are also filtered by `= 'active'`: intended, since only active accounts can hold daily rows, and it matches the live queue's active-only stance.
- RLS (`run_as`) still applies; the new `exists` subselects read `public.profiles` in the same query, like the blocks check, so no new permission shape.

## Open questions

None. The out-of-scope item (running daily games still end on time) is the owner's call per the issue; `ban_profile` needs no change.
```
